What is the DLS method? Duckworth–Lewis rules explained for ODIs and T20Is
stories.summary: Wondering how rain-affected matches are decided in cricket? How the DLS method works in ODIs and T20Is, and how targets are adjusted fairly when weather interrupts play. The DLS method is used to determine fair targets in rain-affected limited-overs matches. The method is exclusively applied to limited-overs formats like ODIs and T20Is and is not used in Test cricket. Many matches, including World Cup games, have been decided by the DLS method, occasionally leading to significant debate. The method's name is derived from its creators Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, including the updated inputs from Steven Stern. Which is how the name, Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method was coined.
